nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light is scarce on the dark forest floor, so canopy trees capture most of it and shade the layers below.

nodes.name: Tropical rainfall
nodes.desc: Heavy year-round rain feeds the rivers and rapids of the Coppename watershed and keeps the lowland forest moist.

nodes.name: Forest soil and leaf litter
nodes.desc: Old, weathered tropical soils hold few nutrients, so the forest relies on fast recycling of fallen leaves and wood.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down leaf litter, wood and dead animals, returning nutrients to the soil for roots to take up again.

nodes.name: Guatteria
nodes.desc: A rainforest understorey tree whose fruits are eaten by birds and primates, which spread its seeds.

nodes.name: Miconia
nodes.desc: A small tree or shrub of the melastome family with berries that many forest birds eat.

nodes.name: Piper
nodes.desc: A shrub of the pepper family. Fruit-eating bats such as Carollia are key dispersers of Piper seeds.

nodes.name: Ocotea
nodes.desc: A tree of the laurel family. Its fruits are a food for forest birds and mammals.

nodes.name: Leafcutter ants
nodes.desc: Cut fresh leaves and carry them below ground to grow the fungus they feed on, making them major forest herbivores.

nodes.name: Seba's short-tailed bat
nodes.desc: A fruit-eating bat that feeds on Piper fruit and spreads its seeds through the forest at night.

nodes.name: White-crowned manakin
nodes.desc: A small fruit-eating forest bird, recorded very often here, that takes berries such as Miconia.

nodes.name: Red-rumped agouti
nodes.desc: A rodent that eats seeds, pulp and fruit. It buries seeds, so it can help plants spread.

nodes.name: Collared peccary
nodes.desc: A pig-like forest mammal that forages in groups on fruit, seeds and roots. Jaguars hunt it.

nodes.name: Red-faced spider monkey
nodes.desc: A large canopy primate that eats mostly fruit and young leaves, plus some insects. A prey of harpy eagles.

nodes.name: Tufted capuchin
nodes.desc: An omnivorous monkey that eats fruit, including Guatteria, and also insects and small animals.

nodes.name: Dyeing poison frog
nodes.desc: A bold-patterned poison frog of leaf litter that eats small invertebrates such as ants.

nodes.name: Ocelot
nodes.desc: A medium-sized forest cat that hunts rodents like agoutis and other small to mid-sized animals.

nodes.name: King vulture
nodes.desc: A large forest scavenger that finds carcasses, including those left by big predators such as jaguars.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: The largest cat of the Americas and the top ground predator here. It hunts peccaries and agoutis among many prey.

nodes.name: Harpy eagle
nodes.desc: A huge forest eagle that hunts sloths and monkeys in the canopy, including spider monkeys and capuchins.
